# `endpoints/auth-route-no-rate-limit`: Login / signup / reset endpoint without rate limiting

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:rules` from the rule metadata in src/rules/. Edit only the
     hand:* regions here; everything else comes from the rule and is overwritten. -->

| Family    | Default severity | GitHub security-severity | CWE                                                                                                                    |
| --------- | ---------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| endpoints | medium           | 5.5                      | [CWE-307](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/307.html), [CWE-799](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/799.html) |

Individual findings can have a lower or higher severity than the default, and each has a
confidence (high, medium or low). Both are explained below.

## What it detects

<!-- hand:detects -->

Custom credential endpoints (login, sign-in, signup, password reset, OTP / magic-link
verification, token exchange) and the server actions that implement them, with no rate
limiter in code. Rate limiters are recognised from `express-rate-limit`,
`@upstash/ratelimit`, `rate-limiter-flexible`, `@fastify/rate-limit`, and names listed in
`endpoints.rateLimitFunctions`. Always **medium** severity with medium or low confidence.

<!-- /hand:detects -->

## Why it matters

Custom credential endpoints (login, signup, password reset, OTP verification) are public by necessity. Without a rate limit, attackers can guess passwords and 6-digit codes, enumerate accounts, and run up your email/SMS bill. Endpoints that delegate to Supabase Auth or Firebase Auth are not reported, because those services rate-limit themselves.

## Messages

What a finding from this rule says (parameters in braces):

- {endpoint} handles credentials and has no rate limiting in code. Limits enforced by a gateway, WAF or CDN are invisible to VibeGuard; if you have one, suppress this with the reason.

## How to fix

Limit by IP and by account (e.g. 5 attempts per 15 minutes) with a shared store (Redis/Upstash), not process memory, on serverless platforms. Return the same response for unknown accounts, and add exponential backoff or CAPTCHA after repeated failures.

### Vulnerable

```ts
app.post('/api/login', async (req, res) => {
  const user = await User.findOne({ email: req.body.email });
  if (!user || !(await bcrypt.compare(req.body.password, user.hash))) return res.sendStatus(401);
  res.json({ token: signToken(user) });
});
```

### Fixed

```ts
import rateLimit from 'express-rate-limit';

const loginLimiter = rateLimit({ windowMs: 15 * 60 * 1000, limit: 5, standardHeaders: 'draft-7' });

app.post('/api/login', loginLimiter, async (req, res) => {
  // … same handler …
});
```

## False positives and limitations

<!-- hand:false-positives -->

- **Managed auth is not reported:** endpoints that only delegate to Supabase Auth or
  Firebase Auth, which rate-limit themselves.
- **Limits enforced by infrastructure** (WAF, CDN, API gateway, Vercel / Cloudflare rules)
  are invisible, which is why this rule never reports high confidence. Suppress with the
  reason.
- **Custom limiters:** add their names to `endpoints.rateLimitFunctions`.
- **Limitations:** endpoint purpose is inferred from route paths and handler names; an
  unusually named login endpoint is not discovered.

<!-- /hand:false-positives -->

## How to suppress

Only suppress a finding after confirming it is safe. Put the directive on the line above
the reported line (or use `vibeguard-ignore-line` on the line itself, or
`vibeguard-ignore-file` anywhere in the file). The reason is required: a directive without
one suppresses nothing and is reported.

```ts
// vibeguard-ignore-next-line endpoints/auth-route-no-rate-limit -- explain why this is safe (at least 10 characters)
<the line VibeGuard reported>
```

Use the comment syntax of the file: `//` or `/* */` in code, `#` in `.env` and YAML
files, `--` in SQL.

To turn the rule off or change its severity for the whole project, use `.vibeguard.yml`:

```yaml
version: 1
rules:
  endpoints/auth-route-no-rate-limit: off # or: { severity: low }
```

See [configuration](../../configuration.md) and
[ADR-0004](../../adr/0004-suppression-design.md).

## CWE

- [CWE-307](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/307.html): Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
- [CWE-799](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/799.html): Improper Control of Interaction Frequency
